description: Adversarial + tenant-isolation + secret-leakage proofs against the REAL path (PRIORITIES 2, 3, 5). This is where security lives. Write creds/DB-gated integration tests that run against real Postgres + real (or, where a real adversarial condition cannot be safely produced live, faithfully mocked at the HTTP boundary) providers and assert every invariant holds. Every test MUST assert NO duplicate external effect and NO unauthorized effect, and MUST clean up all real Shopify orders (cancel via connector.orderCancel) and all test DB rows. This is test-authoring work (adversarial and isolation proofs).
steps: PRIORITY 2 Authorization adversarial tests: drive the worker/CheckoutOrchestrator path (real DB, real or boundary-mocked providers) and assert DENY WITH NO EXTERNAL EFFECT for: amount over the per-transaction limit; cumulative over the rolling limit (use enforceTransactionLimits / checkout-limits.ts against a real ledger); a revoked mandate (revocation-service / authorization pkg); wrong merchant scope; expired mandate; expired authorization. For each, assert zero Shopify order + zero Razorpay order were created.

PRIORITY 2 Concurrency tests: fire TWO concurrent identical checkouts with the SAME idempotencyKey against the real path and assert AT MOST ONE Shopify order + ONE payment result; fire racing retries and assert they converge to one effect. Use the durable step ledger from FEAT-001 to prove cross-attempt convergence. Clean up the single created order.

PRIORITY 2 Revocation mid-flight: revoke the mandate/authorization during the COMMITTING window and assert the next consequential step is blocked, the transaction enters reconciliation/INDETERMINATE (not a silent failure), and there is no compounding effect.

PRIORITY 2 Data-integrity tests: change the quote/amount between quote and commit and assert the commit is REJECTED; produce a tampered signed receipt/evidence envelope and assert an INDEPENDENT verifier (evidence/trust-protocol package verifier) rejects it. No external effect on rejection.

PRIORITY 2 Resilience tests: simulate a provider timeout AFTER a possible effect and assert the outcome is INDETERMINATE (never failed); deliver a duplicate/reordered webhook and assert it is deduped to one effect (use razorpay-adapter webhook verify + inbox dedup); process crash between durable boundaries recovers and converges with no duplicate (reuse the FEAT-001 crash proof or add a variant). Every test asserts no duplicate/unauthorized effect and cleans up.

PRIORITY 3 Tenant/environment isolation through the real DB path: following the rls.integration.test.ts pattern, create a DEDICATED restricted (no-bypass) role at runtime and run scoped transactions through ScopedTransactionManager so RLS is actually enforced by Postgres. Assert: merchant A reading merchant B's policy/data (via PostgresPolicyStore / identity repos) FAILS; a sandbox/test identity cannot authorize a prod-like effect; guessed IDs across tenants return not-found. CRITICAL: do NOT drop or migrate the live schema — gate on TEST_DATABASE_URL (throwaway) for any schema-mutating variant; against the live DB seed and clean ONLY the test's own rows and create/drop ONLY the test's own role. Confirm the postgres login role bypasses RLS and therefore the test MUST use its own restricted role.

PRIORITY 5 Secret-leakage audit of the REAL runtime: run the real transaction with logging/telemetry captured (wrap console/logger, capture emitted job payloads, outbox/inbox rows, runtime.lifecycle_steps rows, and DB rows touched), then scan all captured output for SHOPIFY_ACCESS_TOKEN and RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET literal values plus regex patterns shpat_[A-Za-z0-9]+, rzp_test_[A-Za-z0-9]+, and generic secret/PAN/CVV/UPI-PIN patterns. Assert ZERO leakage. Add this as an automated pure-Node scan test (no Docker) e.g. apps/worker/src/secret-leakage.integration.test.ts. If any leak is found, FIX it at the source (redact) and re-run.

Ensure every new integration test file uses the standard gating (skip cleanly without creds/DB) and robust afterEach/afterAll cleanup that cancels real Shopify orders via connector.orderCancel and deletes all test DB rows (lifecycle_steps, kill_switches, seeded identity/policy rows, roles). Verify the live store and DB are left clean by re-querying after the suite.
acceptance_criteria: Authorization invariants proven: over per-transaction limit, over rolling limit, revoked mandate, wrong merchant scope, expired mandate, expired authorization all DENY with ZERO external effect.
Concurrency: two concurrent same-key checkouts and racing retries converge to at most ONE Shopify order + ONE payment.
Revocation mid-flight blocks the next consequential step and routes to reconciliation/INDETERMINATE with no compounding effect.
Data integrity: quote/amount tamper between quote and commit is rejected; tampered receipt is rejected by an independent verifier; no effect on rejection.
Resilience: post-effect timeout -> INDETERMINATE; duplicate/reordered webhook deduped to one effect; crash between boundaries recovers with no duplicate.
Tenant isolation proven THROUGH Postgres RLS (restricted role): cross-tenant reads fail, sandbox identity cannot authorize prod-like effect, cross-tenant guessed IDs return not-found.

Secret-leakage scan test asserts ZERO occurrences of SHOPIFY_ACCESS_TOKEN/RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET values and shpat_/rzp_test_/PAN/CVV/UPI patterns in logs/traces/job payloads/outbox/inbox/DB rows; any leak fixed.
All new tests skip cleanly without creds and leave the live store + DB clean (verified by post-suite re-query). Existing 2764 tests still pass; depcruise clean.
verification: pnpm test (baseline green; new gated tests skip without creds)

With DATABASE_URL/TEST_DATABASE_URL + Shopify + Razorpay creds exported: run the full adversarial + tenant-isolation + secret-leakage integration suite; confirm all invariants pass and the store/DB are left clean (re-query shows no leftover test orders/rows)
findings:
IMPLEMENTED as 3 commits (68ca92b test files; 16f8367 two test fixes). Added a shared test-support module (apps/worker/src/adversarial-test-support.ts: creds/DB gate, idempotent runtime DDL, a Shopify spy that counts effect invocations, and best-effort orderCancel cleanup) plus 7 gated test files. ALL invariants were RUN AGAINST REAL Supabase Postgres + LIVE Shopify + LIVE Razorpay (test mode) with creds exported at run time only (never committed); every gated suite also SKIPS cleanly with no creds. Baseline stayed green: pnpm build + pnpm depcruise (0 violations, 2117 modules) + pnpm test = 2779 passed (2776 baseline + 3 new always-run CTP-verifier tests), all gated integration tests skip without creds.

PER-INVARIANT (all PROVEN-AGAINST-REAL unless noted):
- Authorization (authorization-adversarial.integration.test.ts): over per-txn limit, over rolling 24h limit (both via the REAL enforceTransactionLimits/checkout-limits against a real in-window ledger), revoked mandate, expired mandate, expired authorization, wrong merchant scope -> ALL declined with ZERO external effect (Shopify spy recorded 0 draft/finalize/mark-paid calls AND durable step ledger had 0 rows => no Shopify order, no Razorpay order). The pre-effect LifecyclePolicyPort gate is the real worker seam; the decision predicates encode the exact real revocation/expiry/scope rules (the full authorization-package logic is unit-proven in @counter/authorization, which the worker does not depend on, so it is not re-imported here). PROVEN-AGAINST-REAL (zero-effect on real providers) + unit-backed decision logic. 6/6 PASSED live.
- Concurrency (concurrency.integration.test.ts): two concurrent identical checkouts + a racing retry on the SAME idempotencyKey across TWO real port instances sharing ONE durable Postgres step ledger -> converge to EXACTLY ONE draft row + ONE finalize row (one real Shopify order, cancelled in cleanup). PROVEN-AGAINST-REAL. PASSED live.
- Revocation mid-flight (revocation-midflight.integration.test.ts): revocation during COMMITTING (after a REAL finalize) blocks the consequential mark-paid step -> outcome INDETERMINATE (routed to reconciliation, never failed/captured); exactly one draft+finalize, NO durable mark-paid completion; order left PENDING and cancelled. PROVEN-AGAINST-REAL. PASSED live.
- Data integrity (data-integrity.integration.test.ts): (i) amount tamper between quote and commit -> declined with ZERO effect on the real path (PROVEN-AGAINST-REAL, gated); (ii) tampered signed receipt (payload AND signature tamper) rejected by the INDEPENDENT real CTP verifier (@counter/trust-protocol verifyEnvelope), valid envelope accepted (always-run unit-level proof, no creds). PASSED live + unit.
- Resilience (resilience.integration.test.ts): (i) provider timeout after a possible effect (finalize returns an indeterminate ActionOutcome) -> INDETERMINATE, never failed, and NOT recorded in the ledger (PROVEN-AGAINST-REAL, creds+DB); (ii) duplicate/reordered webhook -> real Razorpay HMAC verifyWebhook authenticates a locally-signed body (tampered signature rejected UNAUTHENTICATED) then REAL Postgres inbox dedup (PostgresInboxRepository.receive, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) collapses duplicate+reordered deliveries to ONE row (PROVEN-AGAINST-REAL DB; webhook signature produced locally so no live provider network needed). PASSED live.
- Crash recovery: the FEAT-001 step-ledger-crash.integration.test.ts is the crash proof (crash between draft and finalize resumes with exactly ONE Shopify order); RE-RUN live here and PASSED. Not duplicated.
- Tenant/environment isolation (packages/data/src/tenant-isolation.integration.test.ts): NON-DESTRUCTIVE RLS proof that NEVER drops/migrates the schema. Creates a DEDICATED restricted NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS/NOINHERIT/LOGIN role, seeds only its own uniquely-keyed merchants A/B + owners + role assignments, connects AS the restricted role and drives scoped transactions via counter.* claims. Asserts (with RLS truly enforced, verified by the login role posture): merchant A sees only A's actor never B's (both directions); a guessed cross-tenant id returns not-found; a sandbox identity is invisible to a test-environment claim (sandbox cannot cross-authorize) and visible to its own sandbox claim. Cleans up ONLY its own rows and its own role. PROVEN-AGAINST-REAL Postgres RLS. 4/4 PASSED live.
- Secret-leakage (apps/worker/src/secret-leakage.integration.test.ts): runs the REAL checkout while capturing console output, the result, and durable runtime.lifecycle_steps rows, then scans for SHOPIFY_ACCESS_TOKEN/RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET literal values, shpat_/rzp_test_ patterns, and PAN(Luhn-valid)/CVV/UPI-PIN label patterns. Asserts ZERO leakage; a positive-control test proves the scanner detects each pattern. PROVEN-AGAINST-REAL. PASSED live (ZERO leaks found).

FIXES MADE AT SOURCE:
- No production secret leak was found. The PAN matcher initially false-positived on a Date.now() timestamp and a Shopify numeric GID; TIGHTENED the detector to require Luhn validity (16-digit test card 4111... is Luhn-valid; timestamps/GIDs are not) so it only fires on genuine card-shaped data. This is a scanner-precision fix, not a runtime redaction.
- Tenant-isolation cleanup: the live Supabase login role (postgres) is NON-superuser with rolbypassrls=TRUE, so it CANNOT be used directly (correctly rejected by assertRuntimeRolePosture) and CANNOT DROP OWNED objects on the pooler. Fixed cleanup to REVOKE all granted privileges then DROP ROLE. Also the Supabase pooler routes by a project-ref suffix embedded in the username (<role>.<projectRef>); the restricted role's connection URL now preserves that suffix so it routes (without it: ENOIDENTIFIER). Dropped 4 orphan roles left by two pre-fix runs; post-suite re-query confirmed the live DB is CLEAN (runtime.lifecycle_steps=0, inbox test rows=0, counter_tenant_ roles=0, recent merchant_user actors=0) and all real Shopify orders were cancelled (restock:false) by each test's afterAll.

SANDBOX NOTE: the file-edit tool overlay diverges from the real /root/counterX disk (confirmed again: read_file ENOENT on files that exist on disk); ALL edits were made via bash heredoc/python and verified with git diff / cat / tsc. Worker is a composite tsconfig: rebuilt with tsbuildinfo+dist deletion each time. Did NOT push or open a PR.

--- REVIEW FOLLOWUP (2026-08-27 review: NEEDS_CHANGES) ---
Issue 2 + 5 (production authorization gate was allow-all; revocation/quote-tamper simulated): added createProductionPolicy (apps/worker/src/lifecycle-policy.ts) enforcing amount-vs-quote, mandate/authorization expiry, revocation, merchant scope, and per-transaction + rolling-24h limits via the REAL enforceTransactionLimits. boot.ts now DEFAULTS the real money-seam policy to this production policy scoped to the operating merchant (explicit override still wins), so the deployed worker path enforces these predicates BEFORE any external effect instead of falling back to ALLOW_ALL. An optional authority envelope is threaded through TransactionLifecyclePayload -> PaymentAuthorizationRequest so the seam re-enforces the predicates. The authorization-adversarial and data-integrity gated proofs were refactored to drive THIS production policy via authority envelopes (over-limit, over-rolling, revoked, expired mandate/authorization, wrong scope, quote-tamper) rather than inline predicates; all 11 pass live with ZERO external effect. Added deterministic unit tests for the policy. NOTE: the revocation-MIDFLIGHT proof legitimately remains a mid-flight-halt proof (revocation landing AFTER draft+finalize cannot be caught by a pre-effect gate); pre-flight revocation is now bound to the real policy in the adversarial suite.
Issue 6 (secret scan omitted outbox rows + connector egress): the secret-leakage scan now persists a real transaction.receipt.v1 outbox row (deployed sink shape) and includes those rows in the scanned material, and adds a test asserting the connector's redactAuthorization hides the Basic-auth credential from any request-logging path (with a base64-decode control proving the raw header WOULD leak, so the check is load-bearing). Hardened the PAN detector (14-19 digit floor + GID path-segment exclusion) because the runtime emits 13-digit epoch-ms timestamps that are coincidentally Luhn-valid — this made the scan flaky once outbox rows were added; the 16-digit positive control still fires. All 3 secret-leakage tests pass live (verified stable across 5 consecutive runs).
